questions.question_text:
A shape is made up of two circles with the same centre.
The diameter of the larger circle is $30$ cm and the area of the region between the circles is $144\pi$ cm$^{2}$.
What is the exact diameter of the smaller circle?

options.why: Found the smaller radius, $\sqrt{225-144}=9$, but did not double it.
Treated the ring area as the area of the smaller circle, giving a diameter of $2\sqrt{144}=24$.
Found $r^{2}=225-144=81$ but doubled it without taking the square root.

questions.solution_text:
The outer radius is $30\div 2 = 15$ cm.
$A = \pi R^{2} - \pi r^{2}$
$144\pi = \pi(15)^{2} - \pi r^{2}$
$\pi r^{2} = 225\pi - 144\pi$
$r^{2} = 81$
$r = \pm 9$
A radius is a length, so $r = 9$ cm.
$d = 2\times 9 = 18\text{ cm}$

questions.question_text:
A circle has an area of $30\,cm^2$.
What is its radius?
Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

options.why: Divided $30$ by $\pi$ but did not take the square root, giving $30\div\pi\approx9.5$.
Took the square root of $30$ without first dividing by $\pi$, giving $\sqrt{30}\approx5.5$.
Used the circumference formula instead of the area formula, giving $30\div(2\pi)\approx4.8$.

questions.solution_text: Using $A=\pi r^2$, $r=\sqrt{30\div\pi}\approx3.090$. Rounded to 1 decimal place, the radius is $3.1\,cm$.
